intro: Online learning changes the model after each example, so later predictions depend on earlier mistakes. Trace one ordered perceptron pass.
task: Process examples in their given order and update the model whenever its signed margin is zero or negative.
requirements: features is (n,d), labels is (n,) containing -1 or +1, weights is (d,), and bias is a scalar. rate is a scalar in (0,1e6].
For each row, if label*(weights@row+bias)<=0, set weights+=rate*label*row and bias+=rate*label, then increment the update count.
Return {"weights": final_weights, "bias": final_bias, "updates": count}. Use the updated model for the next row; do not batch the updates.

Use real finite numeric inputs with magnitude at most 1e6, excluding booleans. Vectors have length 1..128 and matrix axes have length 1..128 unless a tighter bound is stated. Leave all inputs unchanged; raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.body: A zero signed margin also triggers an update. Count updates when they happen, rather than counting initial mistakes.

explanation: A perceptron adjusts its parameters only when the signed margin is nonpositive. The update moves the score in the direction of the correct label for the current feature vector.
This is one deterministic online pass, not training until convergence. Reordering the data may change the result because every prediction sees the model produced by earlier rows.
